questions.stem: A feeder upgrade C can be supplied by either of two new substations, P1 or P2, with no lag. Which row, written for each year t of C's window, states the rule?

options.text: started_by(C, t) <= started_by(P1, t), and the same row for P2
options.says: One row per parent is "needs all": it refuses a plan with P1 alone, which the rule allows. It cost $870k against $273k for P028.

options.text: started_by(C, t) <= started_by(P1, t) + started_by(P2, t)
options.says: Right: the sum is at least 1 once either substation has started, which is all C needs, as in needs_any for P028.

options.text: started_by(C, t) <= started_by(P1, t - 1) + started_by(P2, t - 1)
options.says: With no lag, L = 0: the parents are read in year t, not t - 1.

options.text: started_by(C, t) <= started_by(P1, t), with no row for P2
options.says: That makes P1 required; any one of the parents is a single row whose right side sums them all.

origin.section: A Child Needs Its Parent: Started by Year t Only if the Parent Had Started by Then

questions.stem: Jobs A, B and C share one crew mobilization: all three start in the same year, or none is done. A may start in 2028 or 2029, B in 2029 or 2030, C only in 2029. Which rows state the rule?

options.text: started(B) = started(A) and started(C) = started(A), with no rows per year
options.says: These tie only whether each job is done; A in 2028 with B in 2030 keeps them, as P008 and P020 did in different years.

options.text: x(B,2029) = x(A,2029) and x(C,2029) = x(A,2029), other years left free
options.says: With A's 2028 variable free, A alone in 2028 keeps every row; years outside the common set must be fixed to 0.

options.text: x(A,2029) + x(B,2029) + x(C,2029) = 3, other years fixed to 0
options.says: This forces the bundle into the plan; an all-or-nothing bundle may also be dropped, as the Ridge bundle was.

options.text: x(B,2029) = x(A,2029) and x(C,2029) = x(A,2029), other years fixed to 0
options.says: Right: 2029 is the only common year, so the members are tied there and every other start variable is fixed to 0.

origin.section: A Bundle That Starts Together Is an Equality per Year

questions.stem: A planner raises child K's lag behind its parent J from 0 to 2 years. J may start in 2029 at the earliest, and K in 2030 at the latest. Neither is a must-do. What does the solve return?

options.text: OPTIMAL, with a plan in which K is never funded
options.says: Right: K's rows force it to 0, the model has another plan, and only a check names the cause, as with P016.

options.text: INFEASIBLE, since K's lag rows can never all hold
options.says: The rows hold with K at 0; a discretionary child that can never start is dropped, not reported.

options.text: OPTIMAL, with K in 2030 and the lag waived by the solver
options.says: A solver never waives a row; every plan it returns keeps all of them.

options.text: OPTIMAL, with J moved to 2028 so that K can still fit
options.says: J has no variable for 2028, outside its window, so no plan can start it then.
